To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Liposomes containing anionic phosphatidylserine and phosphatidyl glycerol, at an equivalent charge density to cardiolipine, are opsonized by the complement proteins iC3b in immunoglobulin depleted human serum.
the liposome-induced complement activation in the absence of IgG and/or IgM is due to C1q binding directly to liposomes.
the classical pathway of complement is activated when liposomes containing anionic phosphlipids at an equivalent concentration of cardiolipin are exposed to serum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the activation of complement by liposomes.
the interaction of liposomes with the classical pathway of complement and the contribution of immunoglobin to this interaction.
the interaction of liposomes with the immune system and the role of immunoglobulin in liposome-induced activation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
immunoglobulin is not required for liposome-induced complement activation, but that it does contribute to the efficiency of this process.
liposomes containing negatively charged phospholipsids can activate complement via the classical pathway in the absence of antibody.
immunoglobulins are not essential for the classical pathway activation of complement by liposomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the classical pathway is activated by anionic liposomes in the presence or absence of IgG and that the IgG does not play a role in liposome activation of the complement system.
immunoglobulin is not essential for the liposome-induced classical pathway activation of complement.
the liposomes become opsonized with complement proteins, but that immunoglobulin does not contribute to this process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
liposome-induced activation does not require immunoglobin.
the presence of immunoglobulines is not required for liposomes to activate the complement system.
the presence of immunoglobuline in serum is not required for the activation of the classical pathway.
